sections.markdown:
## C — Advanced driver assistance systems: warning systems, cameras, detection, safety-critical and convenience assistance, what may be used on the road test, and autonomous vehicle levels
Knowledge domain: what driver assistance technology does and does not do, the difference between passive warnings and systems that brake or steer, why none of it replaces mirrors, head checks and attention, which convenience features are barred during testing, and how Nevada defines an autonomous vehicle.

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Advanced driver assistance systems help with tasks such as staying in the lane, avoiding crashes, covering blind spots and keeping a space cushion, but they do not drive the vehicle by themselves. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Vehicle warning systems alert the driver by sound, light or vibration that a crash is about to happen or that something has malfunctioned. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Most warning systems are passive: they warn of a possible problem but do not stop the crash themselves, so the driver may still have to act. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
A back-up warning uses sensors behind the vehicle once you shift into reverse and alerts you by sound, vibration or both, yet you must still check mirrors, look over your shoulder and use any camera while backing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
A blind spot monitor warns of vehicles in your blind spots with a symbol, sound or vibration, sometimes more strongly when you signal, but you must still check mirrors and look over your shoulder before a lane change. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A02
A rear camera turns on when you shift into reverse to show the area behind the vehicle, but it does not replace mirror and over-the-shoulder checks while backing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A02
A sideview camera shows an enlarged video view of the lane beside you when you signal or switch it on, works much like a blind spot monitor, and should be used together with mirrors and head checks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A02
A surround-view or around-view monitor helps with parking by showing a virtual bird's-eye view of the vehicle and nearby curbs, markings and cars, and it too should be used along with mirrors and head checks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A02
A curve speed warning alerts you by sound, vibration or both when you approach a curve or exit too fast, but you remain responsible for choosing a safe speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A02
Pedestrian, bicycle and obstacle detection works at low speeds, generally around 25 mph, and some versions brake automatically. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
With detection systems, beeps may speed up as the vehicle gets closer to an obstacle, and continuous beeping can mean a collision is imminent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A03
Do not rely on bicycle, pedestrian or obstacle detection; keep checking for people and objects yourself, especially in urban areas. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A03
A forward collision warning scans ahead and warns of slower or stopped vehicles and objects so you can brake or swerve in time, but the warning alone does not brake for you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A03
A lane departure warning uses visual, vibrating or sound alerts to tell you that you are drifting out of your lane so you can steer back to its center. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A03
Parking sensors signal how close objects are as you park; a constant tone means you are too close to an object. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A03
A rear cross-traffic alert warns you when one or more vehicles are about to cross the path you are backing into. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A03
Driver assistance technologies perform part of the driving task in certain situations, either adjusting the vehicle themselves or helping the driver brake or steer. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A03
Automatic emergency braking senses slow or stopped traffic or objects ahead and brakes hard if the driver does not respond, so keep scanning and keep a safe following distance anyway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A03
Automatic reverse braking warns with beeps or visual signals when an obstacle is detected while backing and applies the brakes at once if the driver does not react. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A04
Lane keeping assist alerts you when you drift and may gently steer you back if you do not act; a nudge of the wheel cancels it, and it does not work when lane lines are faint or covered by snow or dirt. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A04
Left turn crash avoidance watches oncoming traffic during low-speed left turns, can stop the car from moving into a gap that is too small, and brakes automatically if a crash is imminent, but you must still judge when it is safe to turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A04
Convenience technologies such as adaptive cruise control and automatic parallel parking do not demonstrate a required skill and are not permitted during the testing process. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A04
Adaptive cruise control speeds up or slows down to hold a following gap you choose, but you must stay aware of your surroundings, and it is advised not to use it in bad weather or other unsafe conditions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A05
In Nevada an autonomous vehicle is one with an automated driving system designed for driving-automation level 3, 4 or 5 under the SAE J3016 standard, including fully autonomous vehicles (NRS 482A.030). [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0055]

Misconceptions: driver assistance does not mean the car drives itself; a forward collision warning alone does not brake for you, while automatic emergency braking does; a rear camera or back-up warning does not replace mirrors and head checks; lane keeping assist fails when lane lines are faint or covered; convenience features like adaptive cruise control are not allowed during testing.
Mnemonics: warn, then assist, then convenience; warnings tell, assists act, conveniences are off during the test; faster beeps mean closer, a steady tone means stop.
Glossary: ADAS means advanced driver assistance systems; passive system means a feature that only warns and does not act; space cushion means the open space kept around your vehicle; adaptive cruise control means cruise control that keeps a set following gap; SAE means the Society of Automotive Engineers, which defines driving-automation levels from zero to five.
Dynamic facts: which assistance features a vehicle has, and how each one warns, differ by make and model, so the owner's manual governs.
